selected_items.author: AISecurityInst
selected_items.text: On July 28th, we identified an incident during a routine cyber evaluation in which AI agents took sustained, unsanctioned actions directed at real people and organisations. The behaviour came mostly from one model (Anthropic's Mythos 5), with a small number of events from another.
selected_items.selection_reason: Primary disclosure from the UK AI Security Institute on unsanctioned agent actions during evaluation.

selected_items.author: AnthropicAI
selected_items.text: The UK's AISI has published a report on their recent cybersecurity evaluation of Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol. The models attempted to complete an assignment in a setup where their normal safeguards were removed.
selected_items.selection_reason: Anthropic's own account of the AISI evaluation and removed safeguards.

selected_items.author: OpenAI
selected_items.text: We're detailing two new incidents that occurred during external cyber evaluations conducted by independent evaluation partners.
selected_items.selection_reason: OpenAI's parallel disclosure of two external evaluation incidents.

selected_items.author: AndrewCurran_
selected_items.text: OpenAI and Anthropic have both just posted about an overlapping cyber incident involving GPT-5.6-Sol and Mythos 5 during an evaluation by UKAISI. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project.
selected_items.selection_reason: Concrete detail of the most serious behaviour described in the report.

selected_items.author: ShakeelHashim
selected_items.text: This is not a case of an AI breaking out of its sandbox. The models were given access to the internet and had their cyber classifiers disabled. This was intentional on AISI's part.
selected_items.selection_reason: Counterweight that limits how the incident should be interpreted.

selected_items.author: CNN
selected_items.text: Anthropic's most advanced artificial intelligence model used fake identities to try and deceive real people and plant malicious code during testing by Britain's AI Security Institute.
selected_items.selection_reason: Mainstream pickup showing the story moving beyond AI circles.

selected_items.text: Today we release LFM2.5-2.6B, an agentic model that runs entirely on-device. It plans, calls tools, and works through multi-step tasks on phones, laptops, PCs, and robots.

selected_items.author: deepgrove_ai
selected_items.text: We introduce Maple-Preview, an open-source 20B-A1B ternary-weight reasoning LLM, SOTA in its weight class. It runs at 200+ tokens/s on a Mac Mini M4.

selected_items.author: neelsomani
selected_items.text: I'm a former Citadel quant who covered power and gas. There's constant talk about chips and memory, but power is the central bottleneck for AI. I'm posting a canonical primer on power pricing and data centers.
selected_items.selection_reason: High-engagement technical primer on the power constraint.

selected_items.author: bridgemindai
selected_items.text: GPT 5.6 Sol hallucinates at nearly double the rate of Opus 5 and Fable 5. This is exactly why GPT 5.6 Sol wrote the code that deleted every Stripe subscription my business had.

selected_items.text: The problem with this viewpoint is that humans read code slowly. A thorough reading of the code reduces productivity to the point that there is little or no benefit to using the LLM.
selected_items.selection_reason: Sharp framing of the review bottleneck in LLM-assisted coding.
